Specify composition allocation blocks

magCompComposition.Rd

Creates a composition specification with one formula per allocation block. For two categories, the first formula allocates among parent categories and the second allocates among child categories within each parent.

Usage

magCompComposition(...)

Arguments

...

Two-sided formulas naming the response category on the left. Conditional blocks use child | parent ~ ....

Details

The category variables are chosen by the user and need not be species or diameter classes. Either the parent or child can be ordered or unordered. Smoothing uses the ordering recorded by magCompData(), not the category's name or position.

For example, use species ~ height and dbh_class | species ~ height + cover. The two blocks may use different covariates and different factor terms. Their category names must match those supplied to magCompData, in parent-then-child order. To reverse the conditioning, reverse the columns in categories and specify the corresponding formulas. This changes the model specification; structured models and their priors need not give equivalent fits in both orders.

A leading block with \(J_A\) categories has \(J_A - 1\) coefficient rows. A conditional block with \(J_B\) child categories has \(J_A(J_B - 1)\) rows: a separate child allocation for each parent. Within a conditional block, factor scores are shared across parents, with separate loading rows for each parent/child stick. Each block can have its own factor rank and anchors.

Right-hand sides use ordinary regression formulas and the markers described in magCompTerms. For a single category, a two-sided formula such as dbh_class ~ height is equivalent to supplying composition = ~ height to magComp().

Value

A magCompComposition object to pass to magComp().

See also

magComp, magCompSmooth; the technical guide's sections on composition in magComp-package.

Examples

magCompComposition(
  species ~ height + factor_nngp(x, y, K = 1),
  dbh_class | species ~ height + cover
)
